headline: Sensex Gains Over 500 Points Led by FMCG and Banks Amid Weak Global Cues

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: FII buying supported the rally in Indian benchmark indices.
Banking, FMCG, and consumer stocks lifted Indian markets higher.
Global cues turned weak as US markets plunged ahead of Nvidia earnings.
Government raised export duty on diesel by ₹2.5/litre and ATF by ₹1.5/litre.
whatHappening: Sensex gained over 500 points while Nifty50 closed near 25,291.
Tata Motors PV slumped 8.7% following a margin outlook cut by JLR for FY27.
US indices suffered severe selloffs with the Nasdaq plunging 2.2% and Dow shedding 700 points.
Cyclone Akvan intensified over the Bay of Bengal, putting Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on alert.
summary: Indian benchmark indices closed higher led by gains in FMCG, consumer, and banking stocks alongside FII buying support. On the global front, Asian and US markets saw sharp selloffs ahead of Nvidia earnings reports. Domestically, Tata Motors shares dropped over 8% after JLR lowered its FY27 margin outlook, while export duties on diesel and ATF were raised.
